summary.text: Jet streams are fast, narrow air currents, and the main ones on Earth flow west to east near the altitude of the tropopause.
They come from the Sun's heating of the atmosphere, which builds the large circulation cells, combined with the Coriolis force from Earth's rotation.
Meteorologists use their location to help forecast weather, and airlines use them to cut some flight times and fuel use.

facts.label: Polar jet altitude
facts.value: About 9.1 km (30,000 ft) above sea level

facts.label: Also found on
facts.value: Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune

items.prompt: A plane flies from the US to the UK and later back on the same route. Which leg tends to be faster?

options.label: Westbound, as Earth turns beneath it

items.explain: The main jet streams blow west to east, and flyers going from the US to the UK met strong westerly tailwinds.

items.prompt: In World War II, Japan put the jet stream to an unusual military use. What was it?
items.explain: The Japanese used the jet stream to carry Fu-Go balloon bombs across the Pacific to attack North America.

items.prompt: The northern polar jet stream is said to "follow the sun." Compared with winter, where is it in the warm months?
items.explain: It slowly migrates northward as the hemisphere warms and southward again as it cools.

items.prompt: Within a jet stream, where do the winds blow hardest?

options.label: Where the air is most humid
Where air masses differ most in temperature

items.explain: Wind speeds are greatest where the temperature differences between air masses are greatest.

items.prompt: Which two ingredients together produce the polar and subtropical jet streams?

options.label: The Moon's gravity and solar wind

items.explain: Solar heating creates the large circulation cells, and the Coriolis force, caused by Earth's rotation, acts on those moving air masses.

items.prompt: In 1944, meteorologists on Guam forecast very strong west winds high up. Why did that matter for bombers raiding Japan?

options.label: The winds would slow them down
The winds would speed them up
The winds would hide them in cloud
The winds would freeze their fuel

items.explain: The forecast high west winds would slow the bombers on their raids.
